Subject: RFP: Pricing details — latency SLA credits & spot reserve pricing

Hi Logan / Marissa,

Thanks for the initial RFP materials. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups specifically on the commercial section before we proceed to the scoring committee:

1) Latency SLA credits: We need the exact crediting formula if 95th/99th percentile latencies slip beyond the target. Do you credit $ or token units? Is it per-tenant or blended?

2) Spot / reserve capacity: For our bursty workloads we want an option to reserve a small spot-pool at a lower per-hour rate but with preemption. Please outline pricing and an example monthly bill impact for a 2K-hour reserve pool with 20% preemption.

3) Conversion assumptions: We requested a token->inference-second mapping for mixed chat/generation workloads so we can normalize across vendors.

Attached the commercial appendix we received; can you return a short write-up and an updated appendix that we can include in the vendor comparison pack by EOD Tuesday?

Thanks,
Jill

Subject: Re: RFP: Pricing details — latency SLA credits & spot reserve pricing

Jill — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two files: 1) Redwood_RFP_Pricing_Appendix_v3.pdf (commercial tables + worked examples) and 2) SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx (line-by-line crediting logic). Summary below for the pack (short version):

• Latency SLA crediting: we apply token-credit offsets (not cash refunds) to make operational impact explicit. Credits are calculated per-tenant monthly, with two buckets:
  - P95 target (<= 120ms): if P95 exceeds target, affected request tokens are credited at 25% of list token price, pro-rated by the excess latency fraction up to a cap of 20% monthly credit.
  - P99 target (<= 250ms): P99 misses trigger a heavier credit: 50% of list token price for affected tokens, pro-rated, capped at 40% monthly credit.

• Practical example (from appendix): a 1M-token month where P99 degradations affected 10% of requests results in a credit equal to 1M * 0.10 * 0.50 * token_price = 50k * token_price (we also show scenario tables in the XLSX).

• Spot / reserve pool pricing: two options we recommend for Acme's profile:
  - Reserved slot pool (non-preemptible): flat monthly price per slot (vCPU/GPU profile) with a 12-month commit discount.
  - Spot reserve pool (preemptible): 35% off the reserved slot hourly rate; preemption SLA: 20% expected preemptions/month. Preemption events are credited as pool-hours and converted to token credits at a conservative 1 slot-hour = 12k tokens for your mixed chat/generation mix (detailed conversion in appendix).

Worked example in appendix shows a 2,000 slot-hour spot pool with 20% preemption => 400 preempted hours credited => 400 * 12k = 4.8M token-credit which is applied at the spot unit price (see table).

• Conversion and normalization: we included a Token-to-Inference-Second mapping based on your provided workload mix (60% chat, 40% long-form generation). For mixed workloads we use: 1 inference-second = 8.5k tokens (chat-weighted), and we show how to convert to cost-per-inference-second for comparison.

If you want, we can provide a second appendix with cash-equivalent crediting (instead of token credits) for scoring. Let me know which the committee prefers.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Internal notes (do not send):

Thanks — solid draft. A few proposed changes before we finalize for Acme:

1) Move P95 cap from 20% to 15% for large enterprise accounts but add a secondary discretionary credit for verified outage windows. Keeps our exposure bounded.
2) For spot preemption conversion use a slightly more conservative 1 slot-hour = 10k tokens for scoring (procurement tends to favor worst-case). We'll include both conservative and optimistic lines in the appendix so procurement can choose.
3) Add an optional cash-equivalent column: procurement may score monetary credits higher than token credits.

Karthik / Ben: can you confirm the slot-hour->token conversions and update the XLSX with both conversion rows (10k / 12k) and a cash-equivalent worksheet? If possible, update by COB Monday so Logan can send the vendor-facing response Tuesday morning.

-Marissa

Jill — following internal alignment, attached is the updated appendix and the SLA-credit matrix (now includes both conservative and optimistic conversion lines and a cash-equivalent column). Highlights of the final offer:

• Latency SLA crediting (final): P95 credit = 25% token-price, pro-rated, capped at 15% monthly for enterprise accounts. P99 credit = 50% token-price, pro-rated, capped at 40% monthly. We keep token-credit primary; cash-equivalent column included for your scoring.

• Spot reserve pricing (final): preemptible spot pool priced at 35% off reserved slot-hour rate. For scoring we provide two conversions: conservative = 1 slot-hour = 10k tokens; optimistic = 12k tokens. Example (conservative) for 2k slot-hours with 20% preemption = 400 preempted hours -> 4.0M token-credit applied at spot unit price.

• Invoice/true-up: token-credits are applied to the monthly invoice as negative line items. Any residual difference after credits can be refunded in cash upon request (subject to standard finance review).

We've also included a short worked example that maps each scenario to a single-line cash-equivalent so your scoring rubric can compare apples-to-apples across vendors. DocuSign/playbook link is in the Drive folder if you want to proceed to terms.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-rfp
